scenario: AI 编码面试里，你要在很短时间内确认 AI 生成的代码是否正确，而不是逐行通读。
q: AI 编码面试中，最强的验证工具是哪两类？
options: 测试和类型系统
更长的提示和更多注释
截图和颜色主题
只读 AI 生成的解释文字
options_en: Tests and the type system.
Longer prompts and more comments.
Screenshots and color themes.
Just reading the AI's own explanation.
why: 测试把正确性具体化，类型系统能在运行前抓住一大类错误，二者都让验证不只靠人工通读。
why_en: Tests and the type system are your strongest verification tools because they make correctness concrete and catch bugs before you read a line.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Verify[Verification] --> Tests[Tests]
  Verify --> Types[Type system]
  Tests --> Behavior[Behavior confidence]
  Types --> Contract[Interface confidence]

termDefinitions.meaning: 编程语言在编译或运行前检查变量类型是否匹配的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A type system is a language mechanism that checks whether variable types match before or during execution.

q_en: In an AI coding interview, which two tools are your strongest verification tools?
scenario_en: In an AI coding interview, you need to confirm AI-generated code is correct quickly, not by reading every line.
optionExplanations: 测试给出可运行的通过/失败信号，类型系统在编译期就能拦下一类错误，两者合起来是最快的客观验证手段。
提示词写得再长也只是生成前的准备，跑不出来就验证不了生成后的代码对不对。
截图只能看界面像不像，看不出后端逻辑或边界条件对不对。
AI 自己的文字解释可能和它实际写出的代码对不上，不能当验证证据。
optionExplanations_en: Tests give a runnable pass/fail signal, and compile-time type checks catch a whole class of bugs — together the fastest objective check you have.
Longer prompts only shape what gets generated; they produce nothing you can run to confirm the result is correct.
Screenshots only show whether the UI looks right, not whether the backend logic or edge cases are correct.
The AI's own explanation can diverge from the code it actually wrote, so it isn't independent evidence.

scenario: 你打算先写好一批测试，再让 AI 按测试去实现功能。
q: 测试为什么会让 AI 生成代码更可靠？（多选）
options: 给模型明确的目标输出
约束模型对需求的解释空间
让你能用运行结果快速验证
保证测试本身永远正确
options_en: It gives the model a concrete target output.
It narrows the model's room to misinterpret the requirement.
It lets you verify behavior quickly by running the suite.
It guarantees the tests themselves are always correct.
why: 测试能约束实现并加速验证，但 AI 生成的测试也可能有错，需要你审查。
why_en: Tests give the AI concrete targets and let you verify quickly, but AI-written tests can still be wrong, so you have to review them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证某个输入是否产生期望输出的一次具体检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A test case is a concrete check that a given input produces the expected output.

q_en: Why do tests make AI-generated code more reliable? (multi-select)
scenario_en: You plan to write a batch of tests first, then have the AI implement the feature against them.
optionExplanations: 先写测试等于先给出具体的输入输出目标，AI 不用再猜你想要什么。
测试把「正确」的定义收窄，AI 更难悄悄按自己的理解跑偏。
跑一遍测试就能拿到通过/失败信号，不用逐行读代码去判断对不对。
别以为测试代码天然不会错——AI 写的用例期望值也可能算错，照单全收会掩盖真正的 bug。
optionExplanations_en: Writing tests first hands the AI a concrete input/output target instead of leaving it to guess.
Tests narrow the definition of correct, so the AI has less room to quietly drift from what you meant.
Running the suite gives a pass/fail signal in seconds, so you don't have to read every line to judge correctness.
Don't assume the tests are automatically correct — a miscalculated expected value in an AI-generated case will hide a real bug.

scenario: 开放式面试中你从空项目开始，要实现一个明确接口。
q: 开始写实现前，你应该先做哪件事？
options: 先让 AI 写完整实现，最后随便跑一下
先针对预期接口写会失败的测试，再让实现去满足测试
不写测试，节省时间
只写注释说明，不写代码骨架
options_en: Have the AI write a full implementation first, then run it once at the end.
Write tests against the intended interface first, then make the implementation satisfy them.
Skip tests entirely to save time.
Just write comments describing the plan.
whenOtherWins: 如果是已有代码里的小 bug，可能先运行现有失败测试定位问题，再补边界测试。
tradeoff: 测试先行的目标明确性 vs 立刻动手写代码的表面速度
why: TDD 让失败测试成为 AI 的目标，也让你和面试官先对齐什么叫正确。
why_en: Test-first development gives the AI a concrete failing target and aligns you with the interviewer on what correct means before any code exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写测试、再写实现，让实现以通过测试为目标的开发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TDD means writing a failing test before the implementation, so the code is written to make that test pass.

q_en: Before you start writing the implementation, what should you do first?
scenario_en: In an open-ended interview, you start from an empty project and need to implement a clearly defined interface.
optionExplanations: 只适合你对需求已经很有把握、愿意事后一次核对的情况；这里从零开始且接口未验证，等于赌一把。
先写失败测试等于把接口契约钉死，AI 照着测试实现，你也能立刻用运行结果验证对不对。
省时间是错觉——不写测试等于没有验证信号，bug 会一直藏到很晚才暴露，返工代价更高。
注释描述不了可运行的验证信号，写完也证明不了实现是否正确，只能当补充说明。
optionExplanations_en: Only worth it when you're already confident in the requirements and fine checking everything at the end; starting from an untested interface, that's a gamble.
Writing the failing test first locks the interface contract, so the AI builds toward it and you get an instant pass/fail signal.
Skipping tests to save time is an illusion — bugs stay hidden until much later, and the rework costs more than the tests would have.
Comments can't be executed, so they never prove the implementation is actually correct — at best they're a supplementary note.

q: 把开放式 TDD + AI 的循环排好：
steps: 让 AI 实现到这些测试通过
和面试官确认输入输出与核心用例
tradeoff: 测试先行的对齐清晰度 vs 直接开写代码的表面速度
why: 先定义正确性，再写失败测试，然后让 AI 实现，最后运行和审阅结果。
why_en: The TDD loop is agree on behavior, write failing tests, ask the AI to implement, then run and review the results.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Cases[Define cases] --> Tests[Write tests]
  Tests --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Run[Run tests]
  Run --> Fix[Fix failures]
  Fix --> Run

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写测试、再写实现，让实现以通过测试为目标的开发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TDD means writing a failing test before the implementation, so the code is written to make that test pass.

q_en: Put the open-ended TDD-plus-AI loop in the right order:

scenario: 你还没开始写代码，先把想测试的输入输出讲给面试官听。
q: 实现前先和面试官确认测试用例，最直接的收益是什么？
options: 能让你跳过手动补充边界测试这一步
能保证 AI 之后写代码不会再犯错
提前暴露需求误解，建立共享的完成标准
能自动帮你想清楚所有边界条件
options_en: It lets you skip adding your own edge-case tests later.
It guarantees the AI won't make mistakes afterward.
It surfaces requirement misunderstandings early and creates a shared definition of done.
It automatically thinks through every edge case for you.
why: 对齐输入和期望输出能在编码前发现歧义，也让后续「测试通过」更有共识。
why_en: Agreeing on test cases before coding surfaces requirement misunderstandings early and gives everyone the same definition of done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入处于极端或特殊情况时的测试场景，如空值、最大值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge case is a test scenario at an extreme or unusual input, such as an empty or maximum value.

q_en: What's the most direct benefit of confirming test cases with the interviewer before implementing?
scenario_en: You haven't started coding yet; you walk the interviewer through the inputs and outputs you plan to test.
optionExplanations: 把提前对齐当成边界测试的替代品是夸大了——对齐只覆盖聊过的用例，边界条件还得你自己另外补。
把对齐当成 AI 以后不会犯错的保证书也是夸大——AI 照样可能在对齐之外的地方写错。
编码前先讲清楚输入输出预期，能在下笔前就揪出理解偏差，双方对「测试通过」有同一个标准。
对齐不会自动帮你想全边界，它依赖你主动提出用例，没提到的角落照样会被漏掉。
optionExplanations_en: Treating pre-alignment as a substitute for edge-case tests overstates it — alignment only covers the cases you actually discussed.
Treating alignment as a guarantee the AI won't slip up afterward overstates it too — mistakes can still happen outside what you aligned on.
Walking through inputs and outputs before coding catches misunderstandings early and gives both sides the same bar for passing.
Alignment doesn't auto-discover edge cases for you — it only covers what you actively bring up, so unmentioned corners still slip through.

scenario: 你已经写好测试，期望 AI 实现函数而不是自由解释题目。
q: 哪条提示最能利用测试约束 AI？
options: 凭直觉写一个你觉得好的解法
顺手把项目重构得看起来更整齐
忽略已有测试，直接从头写代码
让这些测试通过，且不改动现有接口
options_en: Write whatever solution feels good to you.
Casually refactor the project to look tidier.
Ignore the existing tests and start from scratch.
Make these tests pass without changing the existing interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果测试本身还没确认，先和面试官或自己审查测试，不要让错误测试驱动实现。
tradeoff: 测试约束下的目标明确性 vs 开放式探索的解法自由度
codeSample:
Implement `scheduleTasks(tasks, dependencies)` so the tests below pass.
Keep the public function signature unchanged.
Do not special-case only the visible examples.
why: 把测试作为目标交给 AI，会减少它对需求的自由发挥，也让验证路径清晰。
why_en: Prompting the AI to satisfy specific tests while keeping the interface fixed constrains its interpretation and makes verification straightforward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 函数对外暴露的名称、参数和返回值约定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface is the externally visible name, parameters, and return-value contract of a function.

q_en: Which prompt best uses the tests to constrain the AI?
scenario_en: You've already written tests and want the AI to implement the function instead of freely interpreting the problem.
optionExplanations: 只有完全探索性、还没有测试约束的早期阶段才适合凭直觉发挥；这里测试已经写好，交给直觉等于浪费约束。
重构适合已有测试保护、明确要整理代码的阶段；这里目标是实现功能，顺手重构容易碰坏还没验证的接口。
跳过已写好的测试从头写，等于把现成的验证信号扔掉，风险还是要从零验证。
把失败测试和「接口不能变」一起交给 AI 当目标，它照着具体用例写，你也能直接用测试结果核对。
optionExplanations_en: Freeform intuition fits an early exploratory stage with no tests yet; here the tests already exist, so ignoring them wastes that constraint.
Refactoring fits a stage where tests already protect you and tidying is the explicit goal; here it risks touching an interface nothing verifies yet.
Starting over and ignoring the tests you already wrote throws away a ready-made verification signal — you'd have to prove correctness from scratch again.
Handing the AI the failing tests plus a fixed-interface constraint gives it a concrete target, and you can check the result against the same tests.

scenario: 你已经用测试驱动开发（TDD）写完一版实现，测试全部通过。
q: TDD 后，你的主要审查重心会从哪里转到哪里？
options: 从审查实现，转到审查测试完整性和期望值
从审查测试内容，转到完全不再审查
从运行代码验证，转到只读注释猜测
从理解业务需求，转到只看编译速度快慢
options_en: From reviewing implementation lines to reviewing test completeness and expected values.
From reviewing the tests at all to not reviewing anything, ever.
From actually running the code to only skimming comments instead.
From understanding business requirements to only watching compile speed.
tradeoff: 逐行审查实现的细致度 vs 审查测试完整性的效率

rows: 耗时长，难覆盖全部路径
测试本身可能遗漏边界

why: 测试通过只能说明实现符合测试，所以你必须确认测试确实表达了题目的正确性。
why_en: Once tests pass, your job shifts to verifying that the tests themselves correctly express the problem, since passing tests only prove code matches the tests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写测试、再写实现，让实现以通过测试为目标的开发方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TDD means writing a failing test before the implementation, so the code is written to make that test pass.

q_en: After TDD, where does your main review focus shift from and to?
scenario_en: You've finished an implementation using test-driven development, and all the tests pass.
optionExplanations: 审查重心从「实现代码」换成「测试是否完整、期望值是否算对」，因为通过测试只能证明实现符合测试本身。
测试通过不等于可以完全撒手——测试本身也可能写得不完整或期望值算错，不审查会漏掉这些。
读注释代替不了跑代码，注释和运行结果是两件不同的事，不能划等号。
编译速度和代码对不对是两个维度，编译快不代表需求理解对了。
optionExplanations_en: The focus shifts from the implementation to whether the tests are complete and the expected values are right, since passing only proves the code matches the tests.
Passing tests doesn't mean you can stop reviewing entirely — the tests themselves can be incomplete or have wrong expected values.
Reading comments is not a substitute for running code; they answer different questions.
Compile speed and correctness are unrelated dimensions — a fast compile says nothing about whether requirements were understood.

scenario: 你正在给一个新写的函数补测试用例，想确认覆盖是否够全。
q: 哪些类别常出现在一套好的测试里？（多选）
options: 只测一个随机大例子
happy path
空输入或零值
边界值、重复值和非法输入
options_en: Only one large random example.
The happy path.
Empty input or zero values.
Boundary values, duplicates, and invalid input.
why: 标准路径、空/单元素、边界、重复和非法输入能覆盖大多数常见漏洞；单个随机大例子不够。
why_en: Good tests cover the happy path, empty or zero input, boundaries, duplicates, and invalid input — a single large random example does not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入和流程都符合预期、程序应该顺利跑通的标准场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the standard scenario where input and flow are as expected and the code should just work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刚好落在允许范围最边缘的输入，如最大值、最小值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A boundary value is an input that sits right at the edge of the allowed range, like a minimum or maximum.

q_en: Which categories commonly appear in a good test suite? (multi-select)
scenario_en: You're adding test cases for a newly written function and want to confirm the coverage is thorough enough.
optionExplanations: 单个随机大例子规模大不等于边界全，很难复现具体失败原因，挡不住真正的风险。
happy path 先确认最基本功能是通的，是整套测试的地基，少了它没法判断后续失败是新问题还是从没跑通过。
空输入/零值成本很低但很容易漏——很多实现在空数组或 0 上直接抛异常或死循环。
边界值、重复值、非法输入是面试追问最爱问的角落，补上它们能挡住绝大多数实现漏洞。
optionExplanations_en: One big random example doesn't guarantee edge coverage and makes failures hard to reproduce — it doesn't block much risk.
The happy path confirms the basic behavior works at all — it's the foundation the rest of the suite builds on.
Empty input or zero values are cheap to test and easy to miss — many implementations throw or loop forever on them.
Boundary values, duplicates, and invalid input are exactly what interviewers probe — covering them blocks most implementation gaps.

q: 补全常见测试类别：
text: 好测试常覆盖：{{happy path}}、空/零输入、单元素、{{边界值}}、重复值、非法输入，以及有性能要求时的{{规模}}测试。
why: 不必每题全覆盖，但用这张清单扫一遍能发现最容易漏掉的测试洞。
why_en: You don't need every category every time, but scanning this checklist reveals the test gaps you're most likely to miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入和流程都符合预期、程序应该顺利跑通的标准场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the standard scenario where input and flow are as expected and the code should just work.

q_en: Fill in the common test categories:

scenario: 你写完核心测试后，想补更多边界条件。
q: 怎样使用 AI 最合适？
options: 完全相信 AI 自动生成的测试内容
让 AI 补边界测试，但逐条核对期望值和有效性
只让 AI 编写实现代码，绝不让它碰触测试用例
直接删除已经写好的全部测试
options_en: Trust everything the AI auto-generates in its tests.
Let the AI add edge-case tests, but review each expected value and whether it's a valid check.
Only let the AI write implementation code, never let it touch the test suite.
Just delete every test that's already been written.
whenOtherWins: 如果时间只够做核心路径，至少覆盖题目最可能追问的边界，而不是生成大量低价值测试。
tradeoff: AI 生成边界用例的速度 vs 人工逐条审查期望值的可靠性
why: AI 很适合帮你想空输入、重复、溢出等边界，但测试也会继承模型盲点。
why_en: AI is good at brainstorming edge cases like empty input, duplicates, and overflow, but the tests it writes can inherit the model's own blind spots.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  AI[AI suggests tests] --> Review[You review cases]
  Review --> Edit[Edit gaps]
  Edit --> Run[Run suite]
  Run --> Trust[Earn trust]

termDefinitions.meaning: 数值或容量超出系统能表示或处理的上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overflow happens when a value or capacity exceeds the limit a system can represent or handle.

q_en: What's the best way to use AI here?
scenario_en: After writing your core tests, you want to add more edge cases.
optionExplanations: 完全相信 AI 生成的测试等于放弃把关——期望值算错，或用例根本没执行到关键逻辑，都不会被发现。
让 AI 帮你头脑风暴边界用例，但逐条核对期望值和有效性，既借了 AI 枚举边界的速度，又不继承它的盲点。
只有在你完全不信任 AI、时间又很充裕时才合理——大多数场景下放弃 AI 在边界枚举上的效率并不划算。
删掉已有测试等于把验证过的安全网直接扔掉，几乎没有场景该这么做。
optionExplanations_en: Trusting AI-generated tests completely means no one checks them — a wrong expected value or a case that never exercises the real logic slips through.
Let the AI brainstorm edge cases, then verify every expected value and whether the check is meaningful — you get its speed without inheriting its blind spots.
Only makes sense if you distrust the AI entirely and have plenty of spare time — in most cases it wastes the AI's speed at enumerating edge cases.
Deleting tests you've already validated throws away a working safety net — almost no situation calls for that.

scenario: 平台给你的题目自带了几个示例测试用例，你准备开始写代码。
q: 结构化面试自带测试时，应该如何看待它们？
options: 它们一定完整覆盖题目
它们不需要运行
它们通常是起点，不一定覆盖所有边界
只要有自带测试，就不能加测试
options_en: They are guaranteed to fully cover the problem.
They don't need to be run.
They are usually a starting point and don't necessarily cover every edge case.
Once there are provided tests, you can't add your own.
why: 平台测试多半覆盖 happy path 和少量基础边界，你仍应补自己看出的关键条件。
why_en: Provided tests are usually a starting point, not a complete validation suite, so you should still add your own edge cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个边界条件同时出现的特殊情况，比一般边界值更少见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A corner case is a rare situation where multiple boundary conditions occur at once, less common than a single edge case.

q_en: In a structured interview with provided tests, how should you treat them?
scenario_en: The platform's problem comes with a few sample test cases, and you're about to start coding.
optionExplanations: 把平台自带用例当成完整规范是错的——它们通常只给基础场景和零星边界，追问角落照样容易漏。
不运行自带测试等于放弃现成的验证信号，发现不了实现和用例之间的偏差。
自带测试通常只是起步覆盖，不是完整覆盖，你仍要主动补自己看出的边界和 corner case。
补充测试和自带测试完全可以共存，谁都不排斥谁——多写测试从不是坏事。
optionExplanations_en: Treating provided cases as a complete spec is wrong — they usually cover only the happy path plus a few basics, leaving follow-up corners exposed.
Skipping the run on provided tests throws away a ready signal — you'd never catch a mismatch between the implementation and the cases.
Provided tests are usually a starting point, not full coverage, so you still need to add your own edge cases and corner cases.
Your own tests and the provided ones coexist fine — adding more coverage never conflicts with what's already there.

scenario: 题目涉及网格路径，平台测试只有普通 3x3 示例。
q: 你最应该补哪个测试？
options: 完全相同的 3x3 示例
随机改变量名
只测 UI 颜色
1x1 网格或起点等于终点
options_en: The exact same 3x3 example again.
Randomly rename variables.
Only test the UI color.
A 1x1 grid, or a case where the start equals the end.
whenOtherWins: 如果已有测试覆盖 1x1，则优先补障碍物、不可达路径或边界坐标。
tradeoff: 极小规模边界的发现效率 vs 重复已覆盖用例的低回报
why: 网格题的极小规模和起终点重合是常见边界，能快速暴露路径初始化问题。
why_en: For grid problems, a 1x1 grid or a start-equals-end case quickly exposes path-initialization bugs that a normal-sized example won't.
q_en: Which test should you add first?
scenario_en: The problem involves grid paths, and the platform's tests only include a plain 3x3 example.
optionExplanations: 重复已经通过的用例不会发现新问题，任何阶段都不该只重复覆盖过的场景。
改变量名不改变程序行为，根本不构成一次真正的测试。
颜色和路径算法的正确性无关，只有题目本身涉及 UI 渲染时才有意义，这里不涉及。
网格题规模最小、起点等于终点是最容易踩初始化坑的场景，能快速暴露越界或路径判断错误。
optionExplanations_en: Rerunning a case that already passed won't surface anything new — repeating covered scenarios never helps.
Renaming variables doesn't change program behavior, so it isn't really a test at all.
Color has nothing to do with path-algorithm correctness — that check only matters when the problem itself involves UI rendering, which it doesn't here.
A minimal grid or a start-equals-end case is exactly where initialization bugs hide, and it quickly exposes out-of-bounds or path-logic errors.

scenario: 你准备把一个正确但慢的算法换成更快实现。
q: 优化前后最重要的验证动作是什么？
options: 先跑全量测试定基线，每次改动后再跑
直接开始重写，最后统一检查一次
把运行慢的测试直接删掉
只看 AI 给出的文字解释
options_en: Run the full suite first to set a baseline, then rerun it after every change.
Just start rewriting, and check everything once at the end.
Just delete the tests that run slowly.
Only read the AI's written explanation.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有测试，先补最关键的行为测试，再开始优化。
tradeoff: 频繁跑基线测试的时间成本 vs 优化引入回归却发现太晚的返工成本
why: 优化会改变内部算法，测试套件是防止正确性回退的安全网。
why_en: Because optimization changes the internal algorithm, running the test suite before and after each change is the safety net against correctness regressions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Before[Baseline tests pass] --> Optimize[Optimize]
  Optimize --> After[Run same tests]
  After --> Compare[Compare behavior]
  Compare --> Safe[Safe optimization]

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改动之前记录下来的、用来对比的正确行为状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A baseline is the known-correct behavior recorded before a change, used later for comparison.

q_en: What's the most important verification step before and after optimizing?
scenario_en: You're about to replace a correct but slow algorithm with a faster implementation.
optionExplanations: 先跑全量测试立好基线，每次改动后再跑，任何一次改动引入的回归都能被立刻抓住，定位成本最低。
只适合改动极小、你对风险有绝对把握的情况；把优化拆成多步却只在最后查一次，坏了很难判断是哪步造成的。
把「跑得慢」误当成「测试有问题」删掉，删掉的往往正是最容易被优化破坏的行为验证。
AI 的文字描述不能替代跑测试得到的客观结果，任何验证场景都不该只依赖它。
optionExplanations_en: Running the full suite first sets a baseline, then rerunning after every change catches any regression immediately, keeping the cost of finding it low.
Only fits when the change is tiny and you're fully confident about the risk; checking once at the end makes it hard to tell which step broke things.
Deleting a test just because it runs slowly mistakes 'slow' for 'broken,' and it's usually the exact test that would catch what optimization breaks.
The AI's written explanation can't substitute for the objective result of actually running the tests.

q: 补全回归风险：
text: 优化前先跑测试，是为了确认已有行为{{通过}}；优化后再跑，是为了及时发现{{回归}}。
why: 没有基线时，你无法判断失败是新算法造成的，还是原本就坏。
why_en: Without a baseline, you can't tell whether a failure comes from the new algorithm or was already broken before.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

q_en: Fill in the regression risk:

scenario: 你在用类型语言写代码，编译器会在运行前做类型检查。
q: 为什么类型系统也可以看作一种测试套件？
options: 它能证明这个算法本身是最优解
它能在运行前抓住类型不匹配和空值错误
它能完全替代所有业务逻辑测试
它只影响代码格式化风格
options_en: It proves this particular algorithm is the optimal solution.
It catches type mismatches and null-related errors before the code ever runs.
It can completely replace all business-logic testing.
It only affects the code's formatting style.
why: 编译器和类型检查器能把一类错误变成明确、可操作的反馈，尤其适合交给 AI 精准修复。
why_en: A type system catches interface, nullability, and mismatch errors before runtime, turning them into concrete feedback you can hand straight to the AI.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类型系统对变量是否可能为空（null）做的静态检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nullability checking is a static check for whether a variable might be null.

q_en: Why can a type system also be treated as a kind of test suite?
scenario_en: You're coding in a typed language, and the compiler runs type checks before the code executes.
optionExplanations: 类型检查和算法最优性是两回事——类型对了不代表时间或空间复杂度是最优的。
编译器在运行前就能抓住类型不匹配和空值相关错误，把它们转成能直接照做的具体反馈。
类型检查覆盖不了业务逻辑是否正确，类型对了只说明接口契约对了，功能测试还是要跑。
类型错误是真实的逻辑风险，不只是排版问题，把它降级成格式工具低估了它的作用。
optionExplanations_en: Type checking and algorithmic optimality are unrelated — correct types say nothing about whether the time or space complexity is optimal.
The compiler flags type mismatches and null-handling errors before the code executes, so you get specific, fixable feedback instead of a runtime crash.
Type checking doesn't cover business-logic correctness — correct types only confirm the interface contract, so functional tests are still needed.
Type errors are a real logic risk, not just formatting — reducing the type system to a style tool undersells what it catches.

scenario: 编译器报出 line 42 的具体类型错误。
q: 给 AI 的最好提示是哪类？
options: something is wrong
重写整个项目
修复第 42 行这个类型错误，保持接口语义不变
把类型检查关掉
options_en: "Something is wrong."
Rewrite the entire project.
Fix the type error on line 42, and keep the interface semantics unchanged.
Turn off type checking.
whenOtherWins: 如果类型错误反映设计不匹配，应先说明设计问题，再决定是否调整接口。
tradeoff: 具体错误位置带来的定点修复效率 vs 模糊描述带来的自由发挥风险
why: 具体错误位置和约束能让 AI 定点修复，比泛泛说「有问题」更可靠。
why_en: A specific type error with a line number and a constraint produces a much more reliable AI fix than a vague complaint like "something is wrong."

termDefinitions.meaning: 函数或类型对外承诺的行为约定，不只是名字和参数类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interface semantics are the behavioral contract a function or type promises externally, not just its name and parameter types.

q_en: Which kind of prompt works best for the AI here?
scenario_en: The compiler reports a specific type error on line 42.
optionExplanations: 只给一句模糊抱怨，AI 只能靠猜，几乎任何调试场景都不该这么模糊。
用最大范围的改动去应对一个局部错误，只有错误其实反映整体设计问题时才可能合理，这里不是。
把具体错误位置和「接口语义不能变」这条约束一起交给 AI，它能定点修复，不会顺手改坏其他调用方。
关掉类型检查器等于放弃这类问题的运行前验证能力，错误消失了但类型不安全问题还在。
optionExplanations_en: A vague complaint like this gives the AI nothing to aim at — it can only guess, which almost never fits a debugging scenario.
Rewriting everything to fix one local error only makes sense if the error actually reflects a design mismatch, which isn't the case here.
Handing the AI the exact error location plus the don't-change-interface-semantics constraint lets it fix the one spot without breaking other callers.
Turning off the checker removes its before-runtime safety net — the error disappears but the underlying type-unsafe code is still there.

scenario: AI 遇到类型报错时，有时会选择让报错消失，而不是修正根因。
q: AI 为了消除类型错误可能会做哪些危险捷径？（多选）
options: 在 TypeScript 里加 any
修正真实数据模型
加不必要的强制转换
忽略 nullability
options_en: Add `any` in TypeScript.
Fix the actual data model.
Add unnecessary type casts.
Ignore nullability.
why: 这些捷径让类型错误消失但没有修正根因，面试官看到会追问正确性。
why_en: Shortcuts like any, unnecessary casts, and ignored nullability make type errors disappear without fixing the underlying issue, and interviewers will ask about them.

termDefinitions.meaning: TypeScript 里关闭类型检查的万能类型，用它等于放弃该值的类型安全。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In TypeScript, any is an escape-hatch type that turns off type checking for that value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 告诉编译器把一个值当成另一种类型处理，但不做真正的运行时验证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A type cast tells the compiler to treat a value as another type without actually verifying it at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类型系统对某个值是否可能是 null 的显式标注和检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nullability is the type system's explicit marking and checking of whether a value can be null.

q_en: Which risky shortcuts might AI take to silence type errors? (multi-select)
scenario_en: When AI hits a type error, it sometimes makes the error disappear instead of fixing the root cause.
optionExplanations: 给报错的值加 any 等于让编译器不再检查它，报错消失但类型不安全的风险原样保留，之后用到这个值的地方都失去保护。
真正调整接口或数据结构，让类型契约本身变准确，是修根因的正确做法，不属于捷径。
用强制转换让编译器闭嘴，不代表值真的匹配那个类型，转换错了会在运行时才抛异常。
假装值不可能为 null 跳过判空，线上遇到真实 null 时会直接崩溃，而不是在编译期被拦下。
optionExplanations_en: Slapping any on the offending value tells the compiler to stop checking it — the error disappears but the type-unsafe risk stays, and every later use of that value loses protection.
Actually adjusting the interface or data model to make the type contract accurate is the real fix, not a shortcut.
A forced cast just silences the compiler — it doesn't prove the value really matches that type, and a wrong cast throws at runtime instead.
Pretending a value can never be null skips the check, so a real null in production crashes the app instead of being caught at compile time.

scenario: 你可能用 Go、Java 或 Python 写这道题，想知道各语言怎么提前发现类型错误。
q: 哪组语言机制都能在运行前帮你抓住类型问题？
options: 只要用 JavaScript 这一种语言就够了
靠 CSS 的 selectors 选择器语法
靠 Markdown 里的 tables 语法
Go、Java、Python 的静态类型检查机制
options_en: Plain JavaScript alone, as the only language, is enough.
Relying on CSS selector syntax.
Relying on Markdown table syntax.
The static type-checking mechanisms in Go, Java, and Python.
why: 不同语言工具不同，但共同点都是在运行前暴露接口或类型假设错误。
why_en: Go interfaces, Java generics, and Python type annotations checked with mypy all share the same goal: surfacing interface or type assumptions before you ever run the code.

termDefinitions.meaning: Go 语言里定义方法集合的类型约定，编译器据此检查实现是否满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Go interfaces define a set of methods a type must implement, checked by the compiler.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 里用类型参数写出可复用、类型安全代码的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Java generics let you write reusable, type-safe code using type parameters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给 Python 的类型注解做静态检查的工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: mypy is a static type checker for Python's type annotations.

q_en: Which set of language mechanisms all catch type problems before runtime?
scenario_en: You might solve this problem in Go, Java, or Python, and want to know how each language catches type errors early.
optionExplanations: 原生 JavaScript 没有静态类型检查，类型错误只能等运行时才暴露，不算「运行前」的工具。
CSS 选择器管的是样式，跟变量类型或接口契约完全无关。
Markdown 只是文档格式语法，不参与代码的类型检查。
Go 的 interface、Java 的 generics、Python 配 mypy 的注解，各自都能在运行代码前暴露类型或接口假设错误。
optionExplanations_en: Plain JavaScript has no static type checking — type errors only surface at runtime, so it isn't a before-runtime tool.
CSS selectors control styling and have nothing to do with variable types or interface contracts.
Markdown is just document formatting syntax — it plays no role in type checking code.
Go's interfaces, Java's generics, and Python's annotations checked with mypy each surface type or interface mistakes before the code ever runs.

q: 把每个阶段后的验证流程排好：
steps: 完成一个有意义里程碑
运行测试、编译或类型检查
基于最近改动定位并修复
why: 阶段后立即验证能把失败范围限制在最近变更，并让调试有明确假设。
why_en: Verifying right after each milestone confines failures to the most recent change and supports hypothesis-driven debugging.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Change[One change] --> Build[Build or typecheck]
  Build --> Tests[Run focused tests]
  Tests --> Decide{Pass?}
  Decide -->|yes| Continue[Continue]
  Decide -->|no| Debug[Debug latest]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个阶段性完成、值得停下来验证的开发节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A milestone is a meaningful stopping point in development worth verifying before moving on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先提出一个具体的失败原因猜测，再去验证它，而不是盲目试错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hypothesis-driven debugging means forming a specific guess about the cause of failure before investigating, rather than trying things at random.

q_en: Put the post-milestone verification flow in the right order:

scenario: 你打算写完全部功能，最后统一跑一次测试。
q: 把所有测试都留到最后运行，最常见的代价是什么？
options: 最后堆积出现级联失败，已经没有足够时间定位
以为推迟测试反而会让结果更准确
以为 AI 会自动帮你补齐所有剩余缺陷
以为编译速度反而会因此变得更快
options_en: Cascading failures pile up at the very end, with no time left to isolate them.
Assuming that delaying tests makes the results more accurate.
Assuming the AI will automatically finish patching all remaining defects.
Assuming compilation somehow becomes faster because of it.
why: 越晚运行，越难知道是哪一步引入错误，修复成本也越高。
why_en: The later you run tests, the harder it is to tell which step introduced the bug, so the fix cost keeps climbing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个早期错误没被及时发现，导致后续多个阶段一起出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascading failure is when an early undetected bug causes multiple later stages to break together.

q_en: What's the most common cost of leaving all tests to run at the very end?
scenario_en: You plan to write all the features first, then run the tests once at the end.
optionExplanations: 多个阶段的错误堆到最后一起爆发，分不清是哪一步改动引入的，修复窗口所剩无几。
测试准不准取决于用例设计本身，跟什么时候运行完全没关系。
跑测试只是给出通过/失败信号，修复 bug 仍然要人来做，AI 不会因为测试跑了就自动补齐。
运行测试的时机和编译速度是两件独立的事，互不影响。
optionExplanations_en: Errors from multiple stages pile up and surface all at once at the end, so you can't tell which change introduced which bug, with little time left to fix them.
How accurate tests are depends on how the cases were designed, not on when you happen to run them.
Running tests only produces a pass/fail signal — fixing the bug is still on you, the AI doesn't auto-patch things just because the suite ran.
When you run tests and how fast the code compiles are unrelated to each other.

scenario: 一个测试失败，你怀疑循环没有处理空数组。
q: 向 AI 求助前，最好的表达是什么？
options: 这段代码坏了，帮我修一下
我怀疑空数组没处理，请检查这个假设
直接删掉这个失败测试
换一个算法重写，不用解释原因
options_en: "This code is broken, fix it for me."
"I suspect the empty-array case isn't handled — please check this hypothesis."
Just delete this failing test.
Switch to a different algorithm and rewrite it, no explanation needed.
whenOtherWins: 如果错误消息已经明确指出语法或类型位置，可以直接给具体错误和约束。
tradeoff: 带假设提问的诊断精度 vs 直接报现象的省事

rows: 怀疑空数组路径未处理，请验证
报错加具体假设一起给
先诊断根因再决定要不要换

why: 带假设的提示展示你在诊断问题，也能让 AI 围绕具体根因工作。
why_en: A hypothesis-driven prompt shows your reasoning and points the AI at a concrete suspected root cause instead of a vague complaint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先提出一个具体的失败原因猜测，再去验证它，而不是盲目试错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hypothesis-driven debugging means forming a specific guess about the cause of failure before investigating, rather than trying things at random.

q_en: What's the best way to phrase your ask before turning to the AI?
scenario_en: A test fails, and you suspect the loop doesn't handle an empty array.
optionExplanations: 只描述现象「坏了」不给诊断方向，AI 只能从零开始猜，几乎任何调试场景都不该这么模糊。
带着「怀疑空数组没处理」这个具体猜测去提问，AI 能围绕它验证或推翻，修复方向更准。
把不方便的失败信号直接删掉，只有测试本身被证明是错的时候才该删，这里问题根因还在。
跳过诊断直接换算法，换了也不一定能解决具体的空数组漏洞，只有确定是算法级问题时才合理。
optionExplanations_en: Describing only the symptom — it's broken — gives the AI no direction to guess from; almost no debugging scenario should stay this vague.
Naming the concrete suspicion — the empty-array case isn't handled — lets the AI verify or disprove it directly, aiming the fix at the real cause.
Deleting an inconvenient failing test only makes sense once the test itself is proven wrong; here the root cause is still sitting there.
Skipping diagnosis and switching algorithms doesn't necessarily fix a specific empty-array bug — that only makes sense once you know it's algorithm-level.

scenario: 你已经形成了失败假设，但想更快找到根因。
q: 形成假设后，最高效的下一步是什么？
options: 完全等 AI 回答完毕，才愿意自己动手
只靠自己一个人查，完全不允许 AI 参与
一边自己调查，一边把假设交给 AI 并行检查
直接跳过这条已经失败的测试不管
options_en: Wait entirely for the AI to finish answering before doing anything yourself.
Only investigate by yourself and don't allow the AI to participate at all.
Investigate yourself while also handing your hypothesis to the AI to check in parallel.
Just skip over this already-failing test and move on.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题很小且你能立刻定位，直接修复会比开第二条线更快。
tradeoff: 并行调查的定位速度 vs 单线调查的思路专注度
why: 你先形成判断，再让 AI 并行验证，不是外包思考，而是跑两条调查线。
why_en: Once you already have a hypothesis, investigating yourself while the AI checks the same theory in parallel usually finds the root cause faster than doing it serially.
q_en: Once you have a hypothesis, what's the most efficient next step?
scenario_en: You already have a hypothesis about the failure but want to find the root cause faster.
optionExplanations: 把调查完全串行化，人工排查要等 AI 先出结果，只有完全没头绪、必须先看 AI 反馈时才合理。
把 AI 排除在调试之外，放弃了它在快速枚举可能原因上的效率优势，只有明确不信任 AI 输出时才成立。
人工排查和 AI 验证同时跑起来，谁先找到根因就用谁的，两条线互不阻塞，通常比单线更快。
对失败测试视而不见，问题不会自己消失，只是被推迟到之后代价更高的时候暴露。
optionExplanations_en: Making the investigation fully serial — waiting for the AI before doing anything — only makes sense when you have zero leads and need its input first.
Cutting the AI out entirely gives up its speed at enumerating possible causes; that only holds when you distrust its output outright.
Running your own investigation and the AI's check on the same hypothesis in parallel means neither line blocks the other, usually finding root cause faster.
Ignoring a failing test doesn't make the problem disappear — it just resurfaces later, more expensive to fix.

scenario: 面试只剩不到三分之一时间，你在犹豫要不要跳过测试直接交付。
q: 为什么不要因为时间紧就跳过测试？
options: 以为测试会自动帮你写好实现代码
以为面试官压根不关心你的速度
以为测试只适合课后自己练习用
跳过测试通常会在最后三分之一引发更昂贵的调试
options_en: Assuming tests will automatically write the implementation for you.
Assuming the interviewer doesn't care about your speed at all.
Assuming tests are only useful for practicing after the interview.
Skipping tests usually causes more expensive debugging in the final third of the interview.
why: 测试是前期投入，能避免后面被隐藏 bug 和回归拖住。
why_en: Testing is an upfront investment that keeps hidden bugs and regressions from dragging down the final third of the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

q_en: Why shouldn't you skip tests just because time is short?
scenario_en: Less than a third of the interview remains, and you're tempted to skip tests and ship directly.
optionExplanations: 把测试的作用和实现代码生成搞反了，测试是验证工具，不会替你生成实现逻辑。
把「不写测试」和「面试官不看重速度」划等号是错的，面试官通常同样看重最终交付的正确性。
把测试的用途局限在课后练习，否认了它在面试现场同样能快速验证 AI 代码的价值。
跳过测试省下的时间，往往会在面试最后三分之一被更长的调试时间加倍还回去。
optionExplanations_en: This flips the roles — tests are a verification tool, they don't write the implementation logic for you.
Equating skip-tests with the-interviewer-doesn't-care-about-speed is wrong — interviewers usually weigh final correctness just as much.
Limiting tests to after-the-fact practice denies their value live in the interview, where they still verify AI-written code fast.
The time saved by skipping tests usually comes back doubled as debugging time in the final third of the interview.

q: 补全验证时机：
text: 不要等到最后；每完成一个{{阶段}}或有意义{{里程碑}}，就运行测试、编译或类型检查。
why: 这样每次失败都更可能来自最近改动，定位速度会快很多。
why_en: Running checks after each phase or meaningful milestone makes failures much easier to localize than waiting until the very end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个阶段性完成、值得停下来验证的开发节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A milestone is a meaningful stopping point in development worth verifying before moving on.

q_en: Fill in the verification timing:

scenario: 你在决定要不要为这道题额外写一个大规模输入的性能测试。
q: 什么时候应该加入规模或性能相关测试？（多选）
options: 题目有优化阶段
需求里提到大输入或不能超时
任何变量重命名都必须加百万数据测试
你准备替换底层算法
options_en: The problem includes an optimization phase.
The requirements mention large inputs or a time limit.
Every variable rename must come with a million-item scale test.
You're about to swap the underlying algorithm.
why: 规模测试用于确认算法级约束；无关的小改动不需要夸张性能测试。
why_en: Scale tests matter when there is a performance constraint, an optimization phase, or an algorithm swap — not for unrelated small changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用远大于日常示例的输入规模去验证程序是否仍在时限内正确运行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scale test runs the program against a much larger input than the usual example to confirm it still finishes correctly within the time limit.

q_en: When should you add scale or performance tests? (multi-select)
scenario_en: You're deciding whether to write an extra performance test with a large input for this problem.
optionExplanations: 题目设计了「先正确、再优化」阶段时，规模测试是验证优化到底有没有效的客观证据。
需求里写明大输入或时限，这个约束直接决定题目在大规模下还能不能按时跑完。
把和性能无关的小改动也套上规模测试，变量重命名不影响运行时间，加了纯属浪费时间。
换底层算法可能改变时间复杂度，复杂度的差别只有在大输入下才看得出来。
optionExplanations_en: When a problem has a get-it-correct-then-optimize phase, a scale test is the objective proof the optimization actually helped.
When the requirements state a large input or a time limit, that constraint directly decides whether the solution still finishes in time at scale.
Requiring a million-item test for every unrelated small change is wasteful — renaming a variable doesn't change runtime at all.
Swapping the underlying algorithm can change the time complexity, and that difference only shows up at large input sizes.

scenario: 测试全部通过后，你在决定要不要继续逐行核对 AI 写的每一段代码。
q: 有了测试后，为什么不再需要逐行证明每段 AI 实现？
options: 因为测试覆盖了行为，你只需确认测试本身没漏洞
因为 AI 代码永远正确
因为测试通过就完全不需要理解代码
因为面试官不能问实现
options_en: Because tests already cover the agreed behavior, so you mainly need to confirm the tests themselves have no gaps.
Because AI-written code is always correct.
Because passing tests mean you never need to understand the code at all.
Because the interviewer isn't allowed to ask about the implementation.
tradeoff: 运行测试的验证效率 vs 逐行阅读发现的架构/捷径问题
why: 运行测试能覆盖行为，但你仍要读关键部分，确认没有硬编码、类型捷径或偏离架构。
why_en: Tests verify agreed-upon behavior, but you still need to skim key parts of the code for hardcoding, type shortcuts, or architectural drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把本该由逻辑计算出的值直接写死在代码里，只能应付特定用例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hardcoding means writing a value directly into the code instead of computing it, so it only works for specific cases.

q_en: Once you have tests, why don't you need to prove every line of the AI's implementation by hand?
scenario_en: After all tests pass, you're deciding whether to keep reading every line of AI-written code.
optionExplanations: 把「逐行读」换成「跑测试+抽查关键实现」，验证效率大幅提升，剩下的工作是确认测试本身没漏洞。
假设 AI 输出天然无错是不切实际的，AI 依然会犯错，完全不设防会让错误代码蒙混过关。
把「测试通过」等同于「完全不用理解代码」——测试只覆盖你写到的用例，理解代码仍是发现架构问题的方式。
把审查责任的转移错误归因到面试规则，面试官几乎总会追问实现细节，这个理由站不住脚。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping line-by-line reading for running tests plus a targeted skim boosts verification speed a lot — what's left is confirming the tests have no gaps.
Assuming AI output is inherently correct is unrealistic — it still makes mistakes, and zero scrutiny lets wrong code slip through.
Equating passing tests with never needing to understand the code is wrong — tests only cover the cases you wrote, understanding still catches architectural issues.
Blaming this on interview rules misattributes it — interviewers almost always probe implementation details, so this reasoning doesn't hold.

scenario: 已有测试大多通过，但你要新增字符串匹配逻辑。
q: 最该补的测试方向是什么？
options: 只用一个最普通的英文单词代表所有情况
空字符串、单字符、重复字符和不匹配模式
只检查代码格式对不对，不管逻辑
完全不给新增逻辑补充任何测试
options_en: Just one ordinary English word standing in for every case.
Empty strings, single characters, repeated characters, and non-matching patterns.
Only checking code formatting, not the logic.
Adding no tests at all for the new logic.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目是数值边界，则优先补最小值、最大值和溢出相关测试。
tradeoff: 字符串边界覆盖的针对性 vs 单一普通用例的省事
why: 字符串题常在空、短、重复和不匹配路径上出错，这些边界能快速提升覆盖。
why_en: String-matching logic most often breaks on empty, single-character, repeated, and non-matching inputs.
q_en: Which direction of testing should you add most?
scenario_en: Most existing tests pass, but you're adding new string-matching logic.
optionExplanations: 只用一个最普通的例子代表所有情况，普通单词覆盖不到空、短、重复这些真正容易出错的路径。
空字符串、单字符、重复字符、不匹配模式是字符串匹配最容易出错的一组边界，能快速暴露空指针或模式遗漏。
把格式规范和逻辑正确性搞混，格式对不对和字符串匹配逻辑对不对是两件完全不同的事。
新增逻辑完全不做验证，出错只能靠运气被发现，几乎任何新逻辑都不该跳过测试。
optionExplanations_en: Representing every case with one ordinary word misses the empty, short, and repeated paths where string logic actually breaks.
Empty strings, single characters, repeated characters, and non-matching patterns are exactly where string-matching logic breaks, quickly exposing null or pattern-matching gaps.
This confuses formatting with logical correctness — whether the code is formatted well has nothing to do with whether the matching logic is right.
Shipping new logic with zero tests means bugs only get found by luck — almost no new logic should skip testing.

q: 把测试失败后的健康调试链排好：
steps: 把具体失败和你的假设交给 AI 或自己检查
先读失败信息和最近改动
验证修复是否让测试通过且没有新回归
形成一个具体根因假设
tradeoff: 先定位证据再动手的调试严谨度 vs 拿到报错就直接改的表面速度
why: 健康调试不是盲目粘错误，而是从证据到假设，再到定点修复和回归确认。
why_en: Healthy debugging moves from evidence to a hypothesis, then to a targeted fix and a regression check, instead of blindly pasting the error.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Fail[Test fails] --> Read[Read failure]
  Read --> Hypothesis[Form hypothesis]
  Hypothesis --> SmallFix[Make small fix]
  SmallFix --> Rerun[Rerun]
  Rerun --> Decide{Pass?}
  Decide -->|no| Hypothesis

termDefinitions.meaning: 原本正确的行为，因为新改动而重新出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regression is previously correct behavior that breaks again because of a new change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先提出一个具体的失败原因猜测，再去验证它，而不是盲目试错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hypothesis-driven debugging means forming a specific guess about the cause of failure before investigating, rather than trying things at random.
